newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila property should weather peso crisis.
newsitem.headline: Manila property should weather peso crisis.

text.p: The Philippine property market is expected to weather the current foreign exchange turmoil and high interest rates, property experts said on Wednesday.
"I don't think the (property) market will be affected," Robert Torrance, vice president of First Pacific Davies, told Reuters at the start of a two-day forum on property financing.
Prime lending rates of commercial banks have shot up to as high 35 percent this week, around double June levels after the de facto devaluation of the Philippine peso last Friday.
The peso exchange value succumbed to speculative attack, falling by more than 11.5 percent.
However, the local real estate industry relies more on pre-selling than bank loans to fund construction.
Latest data from the central bank showed the total exposure of the real estate sector was less than 10 percent of the total loan portfolio of the banking sector.

"It's still a very healthy market ... It will remain that way, unless people lose confidence in the economy, but I don't think that will be the case," Torrance said, though he said consumers would be more selective in buying or leasing residential and office space.

SGV & Co director Michael Harris said that while the recent uncertainties in the financial market could have a negative impact in the short term, "Manila can still be a very exciting place for real estate."
SGV & Co is the country's top management and financial consultancy firm.
However, Harris said a deeper capital market should be developed to support the growing financing requirements of real estate developers in the future.
He said debt instruments such as mortgage-backed securities should be encouraged as an option to finance property projects.
Aside from debt, Torrance said many foreign property developers have been scouting around for possible joint ventures in the country, which should pump in fresh capital into the industry.

"There is an enormous interest in the Philippines at the moment. We are working with several Singaporean groups, Malaysian groups, Japanese, Taiwanese, Koreans. They're all here looking around ... with tens of millions of dollars to invest," Torrance told the forum.
"In recent months, the market has very quickly turned towards an investment-led market. Speculation is drying up very quickly."
